content:
Hi everyone — I'm also new to Lean, still very much learning.

Early on I kept getting stuck on the same kind of thing: errors like don't know how to synthesize implicit argument, and I had no idea what to do with them. I noticed a lot of people in this community ask similar questions about understanding error messages, so I collected those and organized them into a small project.

The result is a very simple VS Code extension: hover over an error and it shows a plain-language explanation — what it means, why it might happen, how to fix it. That's basically all it does. The explanations are built from real errors in Lean's own test suite, so they're grounded in actual output rather than invented.

Honestly, I'm not sure this is a need other people actually have. Maybe most of you read errors fine after a while, or would rather just ask here. I couldn't find anything that helped me at the beginner stage, so I made it — and I'd be very grateful for any feedback:

  1. Does the explanation make sense / actually help?
  2. Which errors do you see most that aren't covered?
  3. Or if you think the whole idea is unnecessary, that's also useful to hear — I'd rather know now than keep polishing something nobody needs.

It's free and open source (MIT). Install fiersity.leanweaver from the marketplace, or see https://github.com/FIERsity/LeanWeaver

Thanks for reading — and for the patience this community always shows beginners. Any suggestions at all are very welcome.
